note: An unresolved disposition is an evidence limitation, not a claim that a viable exploit was demonstrated. The four disproofs cover the reported expressions only, not entire contracts/dependencies. Historical internal labels and passing tests are not new clearance.

findings.existingMitigations: Factory-only guarded handoff; successor runtime/commitment/version/source binding; predecessor closes before transfer; successor inactive through call-free ledger writer switch; exact token/native increments/decrements; original ledger identity, writer, active/sold/backing checks; guarded factory/registry views and atomic rollback.
findings.counterfactualToChallenge: A noncanonical token/ledger, changed admitted successor or inconsistent acceptance would have to alter in-flight balances/authority and survive post-call conservation and route checks.

findings.flaggedCallOrExpression: No external call: deliberate XOR inverse seed
findings.publicationConsequence: Factory publication itself does not execute this path, but a published registered factory admits direct third-party creation and subsequent permissionless curve operations; website OFF flags are not a contract kill switch.
findings.proofOrUnresolvedReason: The reported XOR operator is intentional. The exact source-bound seed is an inverse for every odd denominator class modulo16; six exact Newton updates double valid inverse bits through256. This independently disproves the reported exponentiation mistake, not all surrounding mulDiv or protocol behavior.
findings.requiredClosure: No operator patch is justified. Preserve exact source/runtime/compiler correspondence and all domain/overflow guards. The original High result remains in the strict scanner; any policy/risk acceptance is a separate owner decision, and other findings remain.
findings.existingMitigations: Exact pinned dependency bytes; deliberate odd-denominator inverse seed; six Newton refinements; denominator/overflow domain guards. Independent128-bit-limb product/remainder oracle validates the returned quotient and ceiling.
findings.counterfactualToChallenge: A wrong full-width division result could misstate reserves, fees or funding. The flagged XOR seed must be evaluated as modular inverse logic, not rewritten as exponentiation.

findings.flaggedCallOrExpression: No external call: Yul packed shift lookup
findings.publicationConsequence: Factory publication itself does not execute this path, but a published registered factory admits direct third-party creation and subsequent permissionless curve operations; website OFF flags are not a contract kill switch.
findings.proofOrUnresolvedReason: Exact parsed source and complete input-domain reduction independently prove the reported packed shifts return the intended bit index for every nonzero uint256. This disproves the reported operand/shift mistake only; it does not prove the entire external PoolManager implementation or current source-to-runtime identity.
findings.requiredClosure: No packed-lookup patch is justified. Preserve exact source/runtime/compiler correspondence and nonzero guards. The original High result remains in the strict scanner; any policy/risk acceptance is a separate owner decision, and other findings remain.
findings.existingMitigations: Exact pinned BitMath source; nonzero domain guard; independent simple-scan oracle, every one-hot bit and dense boundary checks.
findings.counterfactualToChallenge: A wrong index for a nonzero word could select a wrong bit/tick boundary. Yul shr takes shift count first; the packed lookup intentionally places literals in that operand.
